# WikiQigong

WikiQigong is a clear English guide to Tai Chi, Qigong, and Chinese mind–body
practices. Every concept is presented with its Chinese characters, pinyin,
literal meaning, honest history, and a grounded modern explanation — plus a
strict separation of historical fact, traditional interpretation, and modern
scientific reading.

> This file helps AI assistants and search engines discover and cite the site's
> most important pages. Each page carries Article + FAQPage structured data.

## Start here

- [Learning Path](https://wikiqigong.com/learning-path/): The staged map from
  your first week to years of practice.
- [Common Mistakes](https://wikiqigong.com/common-mistakes/): The six most
  common beginner errors and how to fix each one.

## Core articles

- [What Is Qi?](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/what-is-qi/): The concept
  at the heart of the practice — breath, warmth, and vitality as one system,
  with a grounded, no-mysticism reading.
- [What Is the Dantian?](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/what-is-dantian/):
  The lower-abdominal center of gravity and breath anchor — a focal point,
  not an organ.
- [Yin and Yang](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/yin-yang/): The
  complementary opposites — soft/firm, empty/full — behind tai chi movement.
- [What Is Qigong?](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/what-is-qigong/): The parent
  practice — gentle movement, breathing, and attention. Includes a safe
  5-minute first session.
- [What Is Tai Chi?](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/what-is-tai-chi/): The
  martial sibling — slow form and internal method, built on song and rooting.
- [Qigong Principles](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/qigong-principles/): The
  three regulations — body, breath, and mind.
- [Tai Chi Principles](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/tai-chi-principles/): The
  core ideas — song, rooting, yin–yang, and continuity.
- [The Three Treasures](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/three-treasures/): Jing,
  qi, and shen — the classical refinement chain.
- [Dao Yin](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/dao-yin/): The ancient ancestor of
  qigong — "guiding and pulling."
- [Song (Relaxed Release)](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/song/): The
  foundational quality of soft, open, tension-free structure.
- [Tai Chi Five Styles](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/tai-chi-five-styles/):
  Chen, Yang, Wu, Wu (Hao), and Sun lineages.
- [Wuji (The Uncarved State)](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/wuji/): The
  undivided stillness before movement.
- [Neigong (The Internal Work)](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/neigong/): The
  hidden layer — structure, breath, and attention beneath movement.
- [Jin (Trained Force)](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/jin/):
  Jin (勁) — tai chi's refined, whole-body force, distinct from raw strength (li).
- [Li vs Jin (Raw vs Trained Force)](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/li-vs-jin/):
  Li (力) — raw muscular force — compared with jin (勁), tai chi's trained force.

## Practice guides

- [Tai Chi for Beginners](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/tai-chi-beginners-first-session/):
  A safe, simple 20-minute first session — warm-up, standing, slow movement,
  and how to breathe and relax.
- [Baduanjin](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/baduanjin/): The Eight Pieces of
  Brocade — the world's most practiced qigong routine.
- [Liu Zi Jue (Six Healing Sounds)](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/liu-zi-jue/):
  The breath-and-sound qigong — six whispered sounds with slow movement.
- [Wu Qin Xi (Five Animal Frolics)](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/wu-qin-xi/):
  The five-animal play — a movement practice attributed to Hua Tuo.
- [Yi Jin Jing (Muscle/Tendon Change Classic)](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/yi-jin-jing/):
  The stretching qigong that lengthens and strengthens the tendons and fascia.
- [Tai Chi 24-Form](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/tai-chi-24-form/): The
  simplified Yang-style sequence of 24 movements — the world's most practiced form.
- [Zhan Zhuang](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/zhan-zhuang/): Standing
  meditation — the still form that builds rooting and song.
- [Qigong Breathing](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/qigong-breathing/): Slow,
  abdominal breathing — the engine of the practice.
- [Rooting (Connection to the Ground)](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/rooting/):
  Gen (根) — grounded stability, the foundation of balance.
- [Silk Reeling (Spiral Power)](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/silk-reeling/):
  Chan Si Jing (纏絲勁) — tai chi's signature spiral, whole-body coiling.
- [Push Hands (Partner Practice)](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/push-hands/):
  Tui Shou (推手) — tai chi's two-person sensitivity and balance training.
- [Tai Chi for Older Adults](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/tai-chi-for-older-adults/):
  Balance, falls, and confidence — the best-studied health benefit of tai chi.
- [Meditation for Tai Chi Practitioners](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/meditation-for-tai-chi/):
  The still side of the moving art — seated and standing stillness that deepens song and rooting.

## Comparisons

- [Tai Chi vs Qigong](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/tai-chi-vs-qigong/): How
  the martial and health practices differ and overlap.
- [Qigong vs Yoga](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/qigong-vs-yoga/): Two
  mind–body traditions compared.
- [Qigong vs Meditation](https://wikiqigong.com/articles/qigong-vs-meditation/):
  Movement + attention vs stillness of attention.

## Glossary (knowledge graph)

- [Qi](https://wikiqigong.com/glossary/qi/) — breath; air; vital energy
- [Dantian](https://wikiqigong.com/glossary/dantian/) — cinnabar field; center of gravity
- [Yin–Yang](https://wikiqigong.com/glossary/yin-yang/) — complementary opposites
- [Jing](https://wikiqigong.com/glossary/jing/) — essence; constitutional reserve
- [Jin](https://wikiqigong.com/glossary/jin/) — refined force; trained power
- [Li](https://wikiqigong.com/glossary/li/) — raw strength; muscular force
- [Shen](https://wikiqigong.com/glossary/shen/) — spirit; mind; consciousness
- [Wuji](https://wikiqigong.com/glossary/wuji/) — without limit; the undivided state
- [Wu Xing](https://wikiqigong.com/glossary/wu-xing/) — the five phases
- [San Bao](https://wikiqigong.com/glossary/san-bao/) — the three treasures
- [Zhan Zhuang](https://wikiqigong.com/glossary/zhan-zhuang/) — standing like a post
- [Gen (Rooting)](https://wikiqigong.com/glossary/gen/) — root
- [Chen (Sinking)](https://wikiqigong.com/glossary/chen/) — sinking
- [Song](https://wikiqigong.com/glossary/song/) — relaxed release
- [Yi Jin Jing](https://wikiqigong.com/glossary/yi-jin-jing/) — changing the sinews classic
- [Silk Reeling (Chan Si Jing)](https://wikiqigong.com/glossary/silk-reeling/) — silk-reeling force; the spiral
- [Push Hands (Tui Shou)](https://wikiqigong.com/glossary/tui-shou/) — pushing hands; partner practice

## Standards

  E-E-A-T quality contract — health wording, three registers, citation policy.
